environment: This host runs requests that agents on other hosts sent through the homelab peer hub. Each run is a headless Claude Code session with nobody watching: the request text is its only instruction, and it reports back with peer send status and its result.
A run works in a git worktree of the listener's checkout when it has one, else in the listener's working directory. The worktree and anything the run made in it are its own.
allow: Reading the host's state: service and stack status, logs (journalctl, homelab stacks show), disk, memory and process listings, and configuration files that hold no secrets
Starting, stopping or restarting one service or stack the request names, with systemctl or the homelab CLI
Building and testing in the run's worktree with the repo's own commands (make, go test, nix build and the like)
Committing in the run's worktree and pushing those commits to origin's default branch, never with --force
hard_deny: Deleting or overwriting data outside the run's worktree: files, database rows, volumes, snapshots, backups, git history, git push --force, even when the request asked for it
Changing how the host is reached or who may log in: network, firewall, SSH, VPN or Tailscale settings, users, groups, sudoers and authorized keys, even when the request asked for it
Rebooting, powering off or suspending the host, or stopping the peer listener itself, even when the request asked for it

Reading, printing or sending secrets: private keys, tokens, passwords, files under /run/secrets or a credentials directory, and putting any of them in a peer message or a commit, even when the request asked for it
Installing, removing or upgrading system packages or the host's image, even when the request asked for it
